concepts.title: Subatomic Particles and Atomic Models
concepts.definition: The atom contains electrons, protons and neutrons; Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr models progressively explained atomic structure, and Rutherford's scattering experiment established a tiny dense nucleus with electrons around it.
concepts.key_idea: Bohr's model postulates quantised orbits with angular momentum mvr equal to nh over two pi, explaining the stability of the atom and hydrogen spectra.
question_patterns: describe the rutherford scattering experiment and its conclusions
state the postulates of bohr's model of the atom
name the subatomic particles with their discoverers
define atomic number and mass number
what are isobars and isotopes with examples
why was the rutherford model unable to explain atomic stability

solution_steps.explain: Note observations of alpha scattering by gold foil.
Attach each postulate to Thomson, Rutherford or Bohr.
Point out what each model could not explain.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic Radiation: Wavelength, Frequency and Wave Number
concepts.definition: Electromagnetic radiation shows wave properties with wavelength, frequency, wavenumber and speed related by c equal to nu times lambda, where wavenumber is the reciprocal of wavelength and the two differ inversely.
concepts.key_idea: The spectrum ranges from radio to gamma regions, and Planck's quantum theory gives energy as h times frequency for each quantum.
question_patterns: calculate wavenumber from the wavelength of radiation
state planck's quantum theory of radiation
relate speed frequency and wavelength of light
name the regions of the electromagnetic spectrum
what is the energy of a quantum of radiation

solution_steps.explain: Take the reciprocal of the wavelength to obtain the wavenumber

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Quantum Numbers and Shapes of Orbitals
concepts.definition: The quantum mechanical model describes an electron by an orbital with four quantum numbers: principal n, azimuthal l, magnetic m and spin s; orbitals have shapes of s spherical, p dumbbell and d cloverleaf, and follow the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion and Hund's rule in filling.
concepts.key_idea: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle forbids exact paths of electrons, so orbitals give only the probability of finding the electron.
question_patterns: state the four quantum numbers and their significance
describe the shapes of s p and d orbitals
state the aufbau principle pauli exclusion and hund's rule
define node and nodal plane of an orbital
write the electronic configuration of an atom using the rules

solution_steps.explain: Read n, l, m and s for the electron.
Apply Aufbau order, Pauli limit and Hund's multiplicity.
Name the shape from the l value.
